limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses polyacrylamide hydrogels to mimic tissue stiffness, which may not fully recapitulate the complex in vivo tumor microenvironment.
Only a limited number of breast cancer cell lines (MDA-MB-231, MDA-MB-468, BT-549) were used; generalizability to other subtypes is not established.

The causal chain linking matrix stiffness to drug resistance via ILK and YAP is based on pharmacological inhibition and correlation; direct genetic manipulation (e.g., knockdown/knockout) was not performed.
In vivo validation of the stiffness-ILK-YAP-drug resistance axis is lacking.
The study does not explore other potential mechanotransduction pathways that may contribute to drug resistance.
The doxorubicin concentration (3 mg/L) was selected based on preliminary experiments, but dose-response relationships across stiffnesses were not fully characterized.
The sample sizes for patient database analyses are not explicitly stated, and the statistical power may vary.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

claims.statement: Intermediate matrix stiffness (38 kPa) promotes higher survival rates of breast cancer cells after doxorubicin treatment compared to low (10 kPa) and high (57 kPa) stiffness.

experiments_or_tasks: MDA-MB-231 cells were cultured on polyacrylamide hydrogels of low (10 kPa), intermediate (38 kPa), and high (57 kPa) stiffness to simulate different stages of breast cancer tissue stiffness. Cells were treated with 3 mg/L doxorubicin, and survival rates were measured by CCK-8 assay. Ki67 expression was assessed by immunofluorescence. Live/dead staining was performed with Calcein-AM/PI. Apoptosis-related proteins (cleaved caspase-3, PARP, Bcl-2, Bax) were quantified by Western blot.

methods.name: CCK-8 assay
methods.protocol_description: Cell survival rates were measured using cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) after doxorubicin treatment.

methods.name: Immunofluorescence staining
methods.protocol_description: Cells were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde, blocked with 1% BSA in PBST, incubated with primary antibody overnight at 4°C, and stained with Alexa-conjugated secondary antibodies. Imaging was performed on a confocal laser scanning microscope (FV1000, Olympus). Fluorescence intensity was analyzed using ImageJ.

methods.name: Calcein-AM/PI co-staining
methods.protocol_description: Live/dead staining was performed using Calcein-AM and propidium iodide (PI) to assess cell death rates.

methods.name: Western blot
methods.protocol_description: Protein isolation was performed using cell lysis buffer with protease and phosphatase inhibitors. Proteins were separated by 10% SDS-PAGE, transferred to PVDF membranes, blocked with 5% BSA in TBST, and incubated with primary antibodies overnight at 4°C. HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies were used, and bands were visualized by ECL. Densitometric analysis was performed, and protein levels were normalized to β-actin or Histone 3.
